articles.title: AI OVERVIEWS HAVE STEADILY CLIMBED AS A SHARE OF SEARCHES
articles.summary: AI Overviews have become a core part of how people search. AI Mode visits have grown fast, showing how Google is actively pulling users toward a more conversational search experience. ChatGPT's share is declining as Gemini and Claude gain real ground. Referrals, citations, and ad placements are rewriting the rules of visibility month to month.

articles.title: LIGHTHOUSE OR LANDGRAB? HOW TO PICK YOUR AI SALES STRATEGY
articles.summary: AI founders need to choose between two sales strategies: Lighthouse focuses on securing prestigious clients for social proof, essential for new categories. Landgrab emphasizes speed and broad customer acquisition when the market already understands the product. Each strategy caters to different buyer needs and risks, so choosing the right approach can significantly impact success.

articles.title: CODE REVIEW (AS WE KNOW IT) MUST DIE
articles.summary: Code review was built for a world where humans wrote code slowly and reading the lines was how you earned confidence in a change. The companies that rebuild around how software actually gets made now will win because of the operating speed it gives them. AI gives companies more shots to iterate toward the right answer before competitors can plan their way there. It also frees engineers to do the creative, high-leverage work they signed up for.

articles.title: THE BEST PRIORITIZATION IS NO PRIORITIZATION
articles.summary: Prioritization is a trap that wastes time and effort and delivers worse results than just executing faster. Spend more time focusing on building faster. Shift everyone into durable teams that don't have to do cross-business prioritization at all. Manage 'prioritization' through resource decisions to grow, downsize, or split teams.

articles.title: REJECT OSSIFYING YOURSELF
articles.summary: CEOs are responsible for building an enduring company. For the company to grow, the CEO must grow across all dimensions. Instead of identifying your known strengths, chip away at the ossified shell you've been carrying for protection. This will uncover new areas of strength you never knew you could have.

articles.title: IF YOU DON'T TAKE THE WHEEL, YOUR BOARD WILL
articles.summary: CEOs must take ownership of decisions rather than deferring to their boards, as doing otherwise invites external control. Founders should articulate clear strategies on people, product, and financial velocity to maintain autonomy and build board trust. Successful management demands informed decision-making, a strong organizational vision, and a proactive approach to addressing challenges.

articles.title: CODEX SECURITY CLI
articles.summary: Codex Security CLI has been open-sourced. It allows users to scan repositories, track findings across runs, verify fixes, and add security checks to CI/CD. Codex Security helps security and engineering teams find, confirm, and fix vulnerabilities.

articles.title: MCP 2026-07-28 IS LIVE
articles.summary: MCP 2026-07-28 is the largest update to the protocol since launch. It is now easier to deploy and scale remote servers. MCP is now stateless, so it can be deployed on serverless and edge infrastructure, or scaled horizontally behind any load balancer. There is now a formal path to extend the protocol.

articles.title: BENDING SPOON S-1 BREAKDOWN
articles.summary: After their first startup failed, the founders of Bending Spoons were left with $40,000 and a lesson. They thought finding product-market fit involved a lot of luck, while running a software business well was mostly skill. So they spent $10,000 buying an app that already had users. Bending Spoons has now done this more than 50 times, including Evernote, Vimeo, and WeTransfer. Every product gets the same pricing, data, and experimentation system. Remini alone ran more than 1,000 monetization tests. The system behind the apps is really what they have been building.

articles.title: THE BEST CHARITY OF THE NEXT 50 YEARS MIGHT BE A COMPANY
articles.summary: AI-driven wealth may shift philanthropy as tech founders choose to integrate profit with societal good, blurring lines between companies and nonprofits. Some mission-driven companies already tie growth to positive outcomes, such as health improvements or environmental benefits. This trend suggests impactful future social institutions will be profit-aligned businesses rather than traditional nonprofits.

articles.title: WHY COLLEGE DEGREES DON'T MATTER ANYMORE
articles.summary: AI startups increasingly prioritize speed, adaptability, and proven ambition over degrees, while colleges struggle to match technological change.

articles.title: THE YOUNG FOUNDER EXPERIENCE
articles.summary: Teenage founders can now raise quickly, while some incubators still take 15% to 20% for $100,000 and a desk.

articles.title: HE COULDN'T WRITE A LINE OF CODE. HE STILL SOLD HIS SAAS FOR $3.5M.
articles.summary: A nontechnical founder bought a niche Patreon alternative for $6,000, reached 95% margins, and sold it for $3.5 million.
